newsitem.title: USA: Mass. proposal targets dirty Midwest coal plants.
newsitem.headline: Mass. proposal targets dirty Midwest coal plants.

text.p: Targeting pollution from Midwestern coal power plants, Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger has urged 12 Northeast states and the District of Columbia to form a "Northeast Clean Air Compact", officials said Tuesday.

In a letter sent to the 12 governors of the Northeast region and Washington D.C., Harshbarger proposed that the states ban or place a surcharge on power from Midwestern states that allow dirty plants to operate.

The letter is the latest in a long battle between the coal-producing Midwestern states and the downwind Eastern states where more than half of the pollution is caused by outside sources. Harshbarger fears the situation could worsen with deregulation of the power industry.

"As those plants unfairly flourish under market restructuring, they will send us even more of their dirty air," Harshbarger said in a statement. "Today's proposal fires a strong message to the Midwestern power plants and the states themselves that they should not expect to be able to compete in the big Northeast power market unless they clean up their act."
James Milkey, the chief of the environmental policies for the Massachusetts attorney general's office, said the state was also frustrated by federal measures to try to stem air pollution.
"The goal obviously is to clean our air," Milkey said. "We can't really do that without holding the big Midwestern power plants to modern environmental standards."
